title: How can one rule give the perimeter of any square?
description: A letter for the side of a square gives one rule for its perimeter, and the rule is used for a side of seven centimetres. Keeko doubts that the perimeter is the side plus four.
teaching_notes: One idea: the perimeter of a square is four times its side, and a relation written with letters is a formula. Watch for students who add four to the side instead of multiplying.

source: Write an expression for the perimeter of a square with side q, and use it for a side of 7 cm
video_script.why: A learner sees that a perimeter rule written with a letter-number is an expression that gives the perimeter for every side.
video_script.substitution: The book's own square with side q, and then a side of seven centimetres.
video_script.anchor: a square with all four sides equal
video_script.wrong_answer: the perimeter is q plus four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds four to the side instead of taking the side four times; with a side of seven that gives eleven, not twenty eight.
video_script.payoff_line: The perimeter is twenty eight centimetres

final_answer.spoken: the expression is four times q, and the perimeter is twenty eight centimetres

never_show: the perimeter 28 before the answer beat
maths_rules: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 times the side.
video_script.design: One idea: the perimeter of a square is four times the side. Assumes perimeter as the distance round a shape. The square stays on the stage with its four sides coloured. Wrong idea: add four to the side.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a square with its side left unlabelled, and a second square with the side 7 cm

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: a square with an unlabelled side appears
marks.p3: a second square appears with the side seven centimetres

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>The book asks for the perimeter of a square, whatever the length of its side may be.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>It also asks for the perimeter when the side is seven centimetres.
How can we find the perimeter for every side?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a square whose four equal sides are coloured one after the other; an arrow runs once round the edge

marks.g1: an arrow runs once round the edge of the square
marks.g2: the four sides are coloured one after the other
marks.g3: all four sides are marked equal

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>The perimeter is the distance once round the edge of a shape.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>A square has four sides, and each side is met once on the way round.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>All four sides of a square are equal in length.

beats.on_screen: Given: a square with side q ; a second square with side 7 cm

marks.gv1: the square with side q is drawn
marks.gv2: the side of seven centimetres is written for the second square

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, a square has a side of length q.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>A second square has a side of seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for the perimeter ; the perimeter when the side is 7 cm

marks.fd2: the second aim is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find an expression for the perimeter of the square.
<bookmark mark='fd2'/>Then we use it for a side of seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 4 equal sides, so perimeter = 4 times the side

marks.s1a: the four sides are shown as four copies of the side q
marks.s1b: the words 4 times the side are written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>A square has four equal sides, so we meet the side four times.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The perimeter is four times the length of the side.

marks.s2b: the word formula is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>With q for the side, the perimeter is four times q.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>A relation like this, written with letters, is called a formula.

marks.s3a: q is replaced by 7 in the formula

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>To use the formula, replace q by seven.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The perimeter is four times seven centimetres.

marks.ans: 28 cm is boxed beside the formula

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The perimeter is twenty eight centimetres.
For any side q, the expression is four times q.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: q + 4, struck out; the square with side 7 is walked round, four sides of 7 counted

marks.d2: the square with side seven is walked round, side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks the perimeter is q plus four, because the square has four sides.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>With a side of seven, that rule gives eleven, but walking round gives seven four times.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>The four tells us how many times to take the side, so we multiply by four.
